title: 2021 AMC 10A Problem 4
statement: A cart rolls down a hill, traveling \(5\) inches the first second and accelerating so that during each successive \(1\)-second time interval, it travels \(7\) inches more than during the previous \(1\)-second interval. The cart takes \(30\) seconds to reach the bottom of the hill. How far, in inches, does it travel?

solutions.text:
The distance travelled every second forms an arithmetic sequence: \[ 5, 5 + 7, 5 + 2 \cdot 7, \ldots \]

The standard arithmetic-sequence sum formula is \[ n\cdot\dfrac{a_1+a_n}{2}. \] We know the number of terms is \(30\) and the first term is \(5.\) The last term is \[5 + 29 \cdot 7 = 208.\]

Plugging these values into the expression yields \[ 30 \cdot \dfrac{5 + 208}{2} = 15 \cdot 213 = 3195. \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The distances traveled each second form an arithmetic sequence
Find the \(30\)th term, then use the average of the first and last terms
